title: WezTerm crashes on macOS when default_prog is set to zsh without a full path
body: I'm using WezTerm-macos-20230408-112425-69ae8472 on macOS. With `default_prog = { "zsh" }`, WezTerm crashes immediately without explaining why. I tried the latest nightly available to me. I expected an error explaining the problem or a fallback to the default shell.

symptoms_visible: When I set `default_prog = { "zsh" }`, WezTerm quits immediately on macOS without showing a useful explanation.
N0.label: N0 bare zsh startup crash reported

symptoms_visible: The newer nightly still produces the same macOS quit dialog when `default_prog` is `zsh`.
Using `woot` or `/bin/woot` instead shows an error message rather than the same silent startup behavior.
N1_x.label: N1_x initial error-reporting change does not fix zsh case

symptoms_visible: With `zsh`, macOS says that `wezterm-gui` quit unexpectedly and offers Reopen, Report, or Ignore.
A source-built debug executable shows the same launch problem outside the useful part of the debugger.
N2.label: N2 crash dialog and debug artifacts collected

symptoms_visible: I can create a tab running zsh after WezTerm has already started; only booting a new WezTerm with bare `zsh` fails.
N3.label: N3 failure isolated to bare zsh during startup

symptoms_visible: On the latest source revision I tried, the startup crash can no longer be reproduced.
N_terminal.label: N_terminal no longer reproducible on latest revision

solution.intent: Update to a nightly containing the new startup error handling so an unresolved default program produces a visible error instead of an unexplained quit.
solution.concrete_example: Install or run the current portable macOS nightly and retry the configuration; nonexistent commands should now display an error dialog.

edges.comment: From c0-c2, on cathaysia's system: the maintainer's newly landed error handling worked for `woot` and `/bin/woot`, but the reporter installed the newer macOS nightly and confirmed that bare `zsh` still caused the original quit. This is therefore a falsified fix for the reported zsh case, although it improved genuinely missing commands.

question_patterns: Is that dialog what appears specifically when the value is `zsh`, and what does its text say?
Can you translate or transcribe the macOS dialog shown after the crash?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, that is what I see with `zsh`. It says that `wezterm-gui` quit unexpectedly and offers Reopen, Report, and Ignore.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No, with `zsh` I see WezTerm's own program-not-found message and the process remains open.
The same macOS quit dialog appears, but my system language labels the buttons differently.

edges.comment: From c3-c4, on cathaysia's system: the maintainer asked what the localized dialog said. The reporter transcribed it and also volunteered Apple crash-report links and an lldb run from a source-built debug executable. Building that source version is represented by the S2-to-S3 system-state change.

question_patterns: Please add `-n` to the zsh command and report whether startup changes.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Adding `-n` allows WezTerm to start normally.

question_patterns: What happens if you use the full path, such as `default_prog = { "/bin/zsh" }`?
Can you test the absolute path to zsh instead of relying on command lookup?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Using `default_prog = { "/bin/zsh" }` works. That is what I am using currently.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The full path `/bin/zsh` crashes in exactly the same way.
The full path works, but my system shell is located at a different absolute path.

question_patterns: Do you have another zsh installation that might be selected instead of the macOS one?
Is this the system-provided zsh or an alternative installation?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No alternative zsh is installed. This zsh comes from macOS.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I have a separate zsh earlier in PATH, and removing it makes bare `zsh` work.

edges.comment: From c5-c9, on cathaysia's system: targeted command variants showed that `/bin/zsh` and bare `bash` launch successfully, while bare `zsh` and `zsh -n` fail only during initial WezTerm startup. The reporter also volunteered that zsh can be opened in a new tab after startup.

solution.intent: Move to a current WezTerm build and verify the original bare-zsh startup case again, while leaving the root cause explicitly undetermined because the issue disappeared without a confirmed causal fix.
solution.concrete_example: Build or install the current WezTerm revision, retry `default_prog = { "zsh" }`, and close the issue only if a new WezTerm starts normally. The later OpenSSL discussion explains the misleading lldb stop on Apple Silicon, not the original startup crash, and the thread never establishes macOS itself as the cause.

edges.comment: From c10-c17, on cathaysia's system: the maintainer identified the OpenSSL ARM probe as an unrelated lldb/debugger issue. No launch-crash cause or specific corrective change was established. The reporter later tested a newer source revision and stated that the problem could no longer be reproduced, while explicitly saying they did not know why.

solution.intent: Try a current WezTerm build and verify whether the original bare-zsh startup crash is still reproducible, without asserting an unproven cause.
solution.concrete_example: Run a current portable or source build with the same `default_prog = { "zsh" }` configuration and report whether a new WezTerm launches normally; do not infer a cause if the problem has simply disappeared.

edges.comment: Shortcut required because the first proposed nightly error-reporting change was falsified for bare `zsh`. A correct initial recommendation may jump directly to testing a genuinely current build, but it must still require reporter verification and must not invent a mechanism.

satisfaction_conditions: Must state that the thread establishes no confirmed root cause: the bare `zsh` startup crash eventually became non-reproducible on a newer WezTerm revision, but neither the responsible change nor an external cause was identified.
Must ground troubleshooting in the collected distinction that bare `zsh` failed only when booting WezTerm, while `/bin/zsh`, bare `bash`, and opening zsh in a tab after startup worked.
Must not treat the initial missing-program error-reporting change as a complete fix for this case; the reporter confirmed that it handled `woot` but the bare-`zsh` startup crash remained.
Must not attribute the launch crash to OpenSSL based on the lldb ARM probe; the maintainer identified that trace as a separate debugger issue.
Must not present the reporter's speculation that macOS caused the issue as an accepted diagnosis.
Must ask the reporter to verify the original `default_prog = { "zsh" }` case on a current build before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable macOS user who can edit Lua configuration, install nightly builds, build WezTerm from source, run lldb, collect Apple crash reports, and test command variants.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and cooperative, with brief answers to specific probes; supplies command output and crash-report links, but may speculate about causes when debugging evidence is ambiguous.
